groups.title: Ointment (A51701COM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for secondary bacterial infection of burns or injuries.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area 1 to 3 times a day; the amount is increased or decreased as appropriate according to symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment, or if you are pregnant or may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

If hypersensitivity symptoms (redness of the skin and itching followed by local swelling, blistering, severe weeping, eczematous dermatitis, exfoliative dermatitis, hives and anaphylaxis), overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms including fungi, irritation, sensitisation or superinfection appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (D55200ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin A, vitamin D, vitamin E, vitamin B1, vitamin B2, vitamin B6 and vitamin C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, during the growing years and in old age; to relieve dryness of the eyes; for night blindness (poor vision at night), poor development of the bones and teeth and the prevention of rickets; to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain and joint pain (low back pain, stiff shoulders and the like); for beriberi and eye fatigue; to relieve angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis; and to supply zinc.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 12 years and over: take 1 tablet at a time, once a day.
groups.caution:
Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A a day may cause birth defects. Women who are less than 3 months pregnant or who may be pregnant must not take this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have high blood calcium (too much calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a whole-body inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease, kidney stones or severe kidney failure; or if the user is a baby under 12 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have hyperoxaluria (a condition in which excess oxalate is excreted in the urine); if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have impaired cardiac or circulatory function, kidney impairment or low blood protein; if you have gout, or have or have had kidney stones; if you are short of folic acid; or if you have a tendency to thrombosis.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. The vitamin A in this medicine is supplied in sufficient amounts by a normal diet, so do not let the supplementary dose exceed 5,000 IU a day. This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test results. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with oral contraceptives that contain oestrogen, anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and just before or after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry rough skin, painful swollen joints, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), loose stools, red spots, cardiac arrest, reduced central nervous system function, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive problems, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or fluid on the lungs appears, or if a period comes earlier than expected, becomes gradually heavier or the bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C and of zinc; dry eyes; night blindness; bone and tooth development; neuralgia and muscle/joint pain; cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, dermatitis

groups.title: Cream (685900CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the early treatment of recurrent cold sores on the lips.
groups.usage: Adults: apply an amount large enough to cover the affected area right up to its edges, 5 times a day, for 5 days. Start treatment as soon as possible, as soon as the first symptoms and signs appear.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have a skin infection (tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, ringworm, shingles, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice); if your immune system is severely damaged, for example after a bone marrow transplant or because of AIDS; if you have eczematous otitis externa with a perforated eardrum; if you have an ulcer (except in Behçet's disease); if you have a deep second-degree or worse burn or frostbite; if you have perioral dermatitis, common acne or rosacea; if you are breast-feeding; or if the user is under 18 years of age.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if the user is an older person, or if you have hypersensitivity to propylene glycol or have had a reaction to it.

Do not breast-feed while using this medicine. Do not use it in the eyes, the nose, the mouth or the genital area. Use it only on cold sores on the lips or around the mouth. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not use an occlusive dressing without a doctor's supervision.

Consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are being given probenecid.

If dryness or peeling of the skin (common), a temporary burning feeling or numbness (occasional), or — rarely — redness of the skin, pigmentation, inflammation, bacterial skin infection (impetigo, folliculitis and the like) or fungal skin infection (candidiasis, ringworm and the like), folliculitis, boils, skin irritation, stinging, fever, a burning feeling, rash, redness, flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, prickly heat, sweat rash, worsening of a wound, pressure sores, pustulosis, raised eye pressure, glaucoma or blurred vision of unknown frequency appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Because of absorption into the body, reversible suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, Cushing's syndrome, high blood sugar, sugar in the urine and visual disturbance may occur.

groups.title: Capsule (208201ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for impaired exocrine pancreatic function.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and over: take 1/2 to 1 capsule with each meal (20,000 to 40,000 lipase units). Children aged 4 years to under 12 years: take 1/80 capsule per kg of body weight (500 lipase units) with each meal. Swallow this medicine whole with plenty of water during or immediately after a meal, without crushing or chewing it. If it is difficult to swallow the medicine whole or to swallow the capsule as it is, open the capsule and take the contents with a liquid or a soft food (pH below 5.5).
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine or to beef or pork, if you have acute pancreatitis, or if you have an acute flare-up of chronic pancreatitis.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have cystic fibrosis; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if you have gout, kidney failure or high blood uric acid; or if you have hypersensitivity to proteins of pig origin.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are also taking folic acid preparations, acarbose or miglitol.

If abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting, constipation, diarrhoea, abdominal bloating, abnormal bowel movements, fibrosing colonopathy, skin rash, sneezing, watering eyes, bronchial spasm, high uric acid in the urine, high blood uric acid, distal intestinal obstruction syndrome, asthma, hives, itching, or ulcers in the mouth or around the anus appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (D21900ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, low back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruise pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, period pain and pain from injury, and to reduce fever when there are chills and a temperature.
groups.usage: People aged 15 years and over and adults: take 1 to 2 tablets at a time. Ages 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 tablet at a time. Take the dose 1 to 3 times a day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause bleeding in the digestive tract.

Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease should avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day). Patients with cardiovascular risk factors such as high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes or smoking should consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine if high-dose ibuprofen is needed.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had a reaction to it; if you have ever had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age; or if you are 30 weeks pregnant or more.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age for whom the medicine is essential; if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms from a medicine such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching; if the user is an older person; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are 20 weeks pregnant or more, or are breast-feeding; or if you are debilitated or have a high fever.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain; if you have ulcer or bleeding problems; or if you have lost a lot of fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea or cannot absorb fluid.

If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Do not take it continuously over a long period. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

While taking this medicine, do not take other antipyretic analgesics, cold medicines or sedatives. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are being given other medicines such as medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants or steroids, or if you are taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash and redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, bleeding in the digestive tract, stomach discomfort, dizziness or swelling appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

If anaphylactic shock, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) or asthma — which occur rarely — or erythema multiforme or exfoliative dermatitis — which occur very rarely — or photosensitivity reaction, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis of unknown frequency appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (A31100ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for hives, eczema, lacquer rash and itching.
groups.usage: Adults (aged 15 years and over): take 2 tablets at a time. Ages 8 to 14 years: take 1 tablet at a time. Take the dose 3 times a day, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a child under 8 years of age, if you are pregnant or may become pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you have diarrhoea, loose stools, loss of appetite, nausea or vomiting; if you have a weak constitution, a markedly weak digestive system or reduced strength; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 or have had a reaction to it.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with other laxatives, allergy medicines, or medicines containing an antihistamine (motion-sickness medicines, cold medicines, antitussives and expectorants). Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with other herbal preparations (especially those containing rhubarb).

If loss of appetite, stomach (upper abdominal) discomfort, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), thirst or diarrhoea with severe abdominal pain appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Loose stools may occur.

groups.title: Soft capsule (C93700ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, chills (feeling cold and shivery), fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a serious skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis appears, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had a reaction to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if the user is an older person, is debilitated or has a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or have had a reaction to it.

If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with oral medicines that contain an antitussive (cough suppressant), an expectorant (phlegm medicine), another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or — rarely — signs of shock (hives, swelling and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome — severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, redness and burn-like blistering on the skin of the whole body or on the lining of the mouth or eyes), a serious skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, asthma, general lassitude, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever) or ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance and the like) appear, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.
